question: Which document, projection, schema, format and presentation contracts should own all exports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: The accepted conversion vocabulary and hidden-envelope hard cut required reusable Best API and Plate doctrine repair before final design closure.
requirements: Retain the settled parse/serialize, import/export, encode/decode, pure/editor, and hidden-state target without widening the product plan.
Teach the reusable operation-law naming rule at the Best API owner and the semantic-versus-native authority rule in Plate vision.
Regenerate Codex and Claude skill mirrors from source, bump Plate Next doctrine without mass-attesting packages, and prove exact doctrine parity.
Keep the review design-only and preserve implementation and native-viewer proof limits.
evidenceReuse: Reused the immediately preceding source-fingerprinted export review and design outcome for the product decision. This closure inspected the owning Best API rule, Plate vision serialization doctrine, generated Codex and Claude mirrors, Plate Next version law, and current package attestations. It changed no product source or accepted call shape.
summary: Reaffirm the smaller conversion API and close its reusable doctrine repair. Text syntax uses parse/serialize with complete-document defaults and explicit slice/inline suffixes; package workflows use import/export; encode/decode remains for typed pairs. Semantic interchange carries hidden native state only for a proven independent job with one authority, so HTML/Markdown authored envelopes stay cut while authored JSON and DOCX retain their distinct jobs. Best API and Plate vision now teach that law, generated mirrors are synchronized, and Plate Next doctrine v238 records it without changing package attestations.

Current product code still exposes the superseded HTML/Markdown envelopes and exportToDocx name until execution.
